correctness_confidence.basis: All three theorems, polynomial identities (4)-(5) and (13), parity/rigidity steps (Steps 1-4 of Theorem 1 and Seidel trace divisibility in Theorem 2), explicit Cayley circulants U5 and U7, Table 1 entries, and the 2K_{3,3} complement spectrum counts in Theorem 3(b) were audited directly against the PDF and verified without error.

novelty.basis: Proving the unconditional 1/sqrt(d-1) lower bound and full conference-matrix rigidity for arbitrary orthogonal matrices in O(4k+2) without assuming zero diagonals, along with the pure-polynomial secant bound 2/sqrt(4d-3) and Seidel-spectrum proof of unique tightness at d=3, are crisp original contributions; Belevitch/Paley classifications and the MUB-6 cyclotomic search build on known foundations.

reproducibility.basis: All proofs and explicit rational witnesses (C10/3, C26/5, U5, U7) are completely self-contained in the manuscript, and the split between the 20-theorem Lean 4.36.0 scalar kernel and the zero-float Python certificates is transparently documented; external repository artifacts were not inspected in this PDF-only audit.

rigor.basis: Arguments are elementary, self-contained, and completely rigorous, closing every partial-zero subcase (|N0| >= 3, |N0| = 1, |N0| = 2) in Theorem 1(b) and clearly delineating which matrix-level steps are proved on paper versus machine-checked in Lean.

significance.basis: Resolves orthogonal minimax coherence across conference-matrix orders and establishes strict gaps at all Belevitch-obstructed orders and all odd d >= 5, yielding sharp quantitative lower bounds on real approximate MUB defects.

summary: The manuscript establishes sharp minimax coherence bounds for real orthogonal matrices outside Hadamard orders. For d = 4k+2 >= 6 (Theorem 1), it proves ||U||_max >= 1/sqrt(d-1) with equality if and only if sqrt(d-1)U is a conference matrix up to column permutation, yielding an exact dichotomy between conference-matrix orders and Belevitch-obstructed orders where d-1 is not a sum of two squares. For odd d >= 3 (Theorem 2), a secant linearization yields ||U||_max >= 2/sqrt(4d-3), with Seidel spectral divisibility proving equality holds uniquely at d=3 and strict inequality holds for all odd d >= 5, complemented by explicit rational skew-Cayley circulants in SO(5, Q) (mu = 6/11) and SO(7, Q) (mu = 1188/2437) improving Householder bounds. Theorem 3 translates these results to real two-basis MUB coherence excesses and reports an exhaustive exact Z[zeta_24] meet-in-the-middle search over 24^5 vectors unbiased to {I_6, F_6}, finding 12 rays forming 4 bases with distinct-ray squared overlaps in {0, 1/3} and none at 1/6.
strengths: Complete, elementary, calculus-free proof of Theorem 1(a)-(b), closing all partial-zero row regimes (|N0| >= 3, |N0| = 1, |N0| = 2) to establish full conference-matrix rigidity for arbitrary U in O(4k+2).
Sharp polynomial secant bound 2/sqrt(4d-3) for odd d >= 3 with an elegant reduction of the equality locus to S^2 + S = (d-1)I_d and s | 3, proving unique attainment at d = 3.
Explicit, verifiable rational skew-Cayley circulant witnesses U5 in SO(5, Q) (6/11 < 3/5) and U7 in SO(7, Q) (1188/2437 < 5/7) that strictly beat Householder reflections.

Honest, unambiguous scoping in Section 5 separating the 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 scalar/parity/divisibility/witness theorems from the paper proofs of matrix aggregation/spectral steps and the Layer 2 zero-float Python certificates.
weaknesses: Exact values of mu_R(d) remain open for all odd d >= 5 (only bounding mu_R(5) in (2/sqrt(17), 6/11]) and for Belevitch-obstructed orders such as d = 22, and the rational circulant construction is only given for d = 5, 7 rather than a general odd-d family.
The Lean 4.36.0 formalization covers only the scalar-algebraic, parity, divisibility, and exact-witness arithmetic kernel rather than end-to-end matrix-level proofs of Theorems 1-3.

Minor omission of the one-line determinant step (det S = -2 => s_12 s_13 s_23 = -1) showing S = -(J_3 - I_3) up to diagonal sign conjugation at d = 3 on page 7, and minor line-wrapping breaks inside long texttt filenames on page 9.
strong_novelty_candidates: Theorem 1(b): Complete conference-matrix rigidity for arbitrary orthogonal matrices U in O(4k+2) achieving 1/sqrt(d-1), including the parity-based elimination of |N0| >= 3 and |N0| = 2.
Theorem 2(a)-(b): Pure-polynomial secant lower bound 2/sqrt(4d-3) for odd dimensions and Seidel-matrix spectral-divisibility proof that equality holds exclusively at d = 3.
Theorem 2(c): Explicit rational skew-Cayley circulant witnesses U5 in SO(5, Q) and U7 in SO(7, Q) strictly outperforming Householder reflections.
